annotations.title: Every verse a word occurs in

description: List every verse where one Hebrew or Greek word occurs, by its Strong's number: a concordance. Each verse comes with its text and, where the interlinear has it, `original`: the word as written in that verse, its transliteration, its gloss there and its grammatical parse there. Use it to see how Scripture itself uses a word, and to find passages that explain each other by sharing one (2 Samuel 24:1 and 1 Chronicles 21:1 both use H5496, "moved" and "provoked"). `total` counts VERSES (in `book`, when given); `uses_in_scripture` counts every use of the word in the whole Bible, since one verse can hold it twice (each verse's `original` lists every use there). Up to 40 verses come back per call, in canonical order. When there is more than one page, `by_book` shows where all the verses fall; call again with `next_offset`, or pass `book` to read one book. Pass `followed_by` to find a phrase in the original, whatever the English: H1121 followed by H430 is bᵉnê hāʼĕlōhîm, "sons of God" (Genesis 6:2, Job 1:6); add `gap` to allow words between. Verse text is in the user's conversation language by default; `lang` overrides. Outside trulyrandomverse.com/ai the default edition is the KJV ('english'); pass `lang` for another. Editions whose licence does not allow redistribution are refused. Book, chapter and verse are always KJV numbering, in every edition: the text returned is that edition's rendering of the same KJV verse. A few editions number some chapters differently in print (Ukrainian, Douay-Rheims, Geneva, Swedish and Serbian, mostly in Psalms), so a reader quoting their own Bible's number there may mean a neighbouring KJV verse.

book.description: Optional. Only this book's verses, e.g. "Job".

followed_by.description: Optional. One or more Strong's numbers, in order: only verses where each comes straight after the one before in the Hebrew or Greek word order, starting from `strongs_number`. E.g. strongs_number "H1121", followed_by "H430" (sons of God); strongs_number "H3068", followed_by "H430 H6635" (the LORD God of hosts). Up to 4 numbers. Each verse's `original` then holds the phrase's words.

gap.description: Optional, with followed_by. How many words may stand between each number of the phrase and the next (0 to 5; default 0, side by side). `original` then includes the words between.

lang.description: Optional. Internal language code for the verse text (e.g. 'english', 'spanish'). Defaults to the user's conversation language.

offset.description: Optional. Skip this many verses; pass the `next_offset` a previous call returned.
